messages:
sam: Heads-up — nightly perf regression on matmul-heavy e2e tests after the kernel-selection heuristic change. p99 token latency +18% on raptor-prod trace. I ran nsys and perfetto, attaching quick notes below.

maria: Ugh. Is this the patch that biases cuBLASLt towards larger algos for short sequences? Can you paste the nsys stats?

sam: nsys summary snippet:```nsys profile --output matmul_regress ./run_perf.sh```
GRD: GPU time breakdown: 1) cublasLtMatmul(ALGO_8) 42% 2) cublasLtMatmul(ALGO_6) 18% 3) cudaMemcpyAsync 20% 4) kernel-launch overhead 6%
Top thing that jumped vs baseline is the ALGO_8 path + memcpy.

kevin: ALGO_8 requires a large workspace (reported ~230MB). If the runtime tries to pick it but workspacealloc fails we can hit two problems: fallback to a slower algo + extra memcpy for tiling. Did nsys show workspaceAlloc failures or syncs?

sam: Perfetto timeline shows repeated host-device syncs right when we switch sequences in a batch. There's a pattern: for batches with mixed seq lengths we end up allocating/freeing big workspaces frequently. snippet:```timeline: host->device sync spikes at 0.9s, 1.6s, 2.4s aligned with batch boundaries; memcpy peaks concurrent with ALGO_8 kernels```

alex: That fits the KV cache behavior we saw — variable seq-length batching causes KV cache thrash and forces re-materialization of KV tensors which in turn fragments GPU memory, so workspace allocator can't reserve contiguous chunk for ALGO_8 and we pay fallbacks + memcpy.

maria: So root causes: 1) kernel-selection heuristic overly greedy for ALGO_8, 2) batching heuristics produce high seq-length variance, 3) allocator fragmentation leads to workspace failures and memcpy overhead.

kevin: Quick ablation plan: revert heuristic -> run controlled perfetto run with fixed seq-length distribution; then try forcing workspace cap (set env REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_CAP=128MB) to force earlier algo pick and measure.

sam: I created a repro job:```./bench_tool --workload=causal --batch-distrib=zipf(0.8) --seq-max=2048 --nsys``` Runs at: https://perf.redwood/trace/1769154321-matmul-probe (perf-bot link below)

perf-bot: Automated trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/trace/1769154321-matmul-probe (nsys + perfetto layers). Summary: workspace alloc failures: 11, avg memcpy per-batch: 6.2MB, fallback algo occurrences: 18.

alex: For immediate mitigation we can: (A) clamp batch grouping by seq-length percentiles (e.g., split batches when p95/p50 ratio > 2), (B) add a workspace cap env to kernel selector to avoid choosing algos that often fail, (C) preallocate per-worker slab for cublas workspaces to reduce fragmentation.

maria: I can prototype (B) and (C) tomorrow. Kevin can you run the ablation with REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_CAP=128MB and the clamped-batching config? Post results.

kevin: On it. Starting ablation now. Will post perfetto link when done. ETA ~40m.

sam: Thanks. Also adding a quick perf test to CI: when an ALGO selection causes >10% fallback rate in nightly, fail the build so this regressions catch earlier.

maria: Agreed. Add a small unit that runs the deterministic short-seq workload and asserts workspace-fallback ratio < 5%.

kevin: ablation run complete: https://perf.redwood/trace/1769154602-ablation (summary: p99 back down ~3%, fallback rate -> 3% with workspace_cap=128MB + clamped batching).

alex: Nice. Let's land the workspace-cap and batching clamp as a safe fallback, then we can iterate on a smarter allocator to enable ALGO_8 reliably.

sam: Filed follow-ups: RD-2034 (workspace cap in selector), RD-2035 (batching clamp), RD-2036 (prealloc slab allocator). Assigning to maria/kevin/alex. Closing for now, will watch nightly.
